rows.title: TRUNK-6768: Remove unused BOM entries and ban SNAPSHOT dependencies in release builds
rows.excerpt:
on):
- `jaxen` — required transitively by the `liquibase` module for XML changelog XPath support; not declared by `api`/`web`/`webapp`
- `netty-bom` — pins the Netty version pulled in transitively via the AWS SDK S3 client
- `sonar-jacoco-listeners` — used as a listener dependency for the jacoco-maven-plugin / Sonar coverage integration in the root pom.xml, not a direct project dependency

### 2. Release-build check for SNAPSHOT dependencies (`pom.xml`)

Added a `release` Maven profile using the built-in `banDynamicVersions` Enforcer rule, bound to the `validate` phase, which fails the build if any resolved dependency has a SNAPSHOT version, a version range, or a LATEST/RELEASE placeholder.

Tested:
- `mvn validate -pl api` → passes (normal dev builds unaffected)
- `mvn validate -Prelease -pl api` → fails with a precise message naming the offending SNAPSHOT dependency

### 3. What's NOT included, and why

The ticket also asks for milestone (`-M`), alpha, beta, and RC qualifiers to be banned in release builds. I was unable to implement this with `bannedDependencies` (the rule the ticket suggests) or any other built-in Enforcer rule:

- `banDynamicVersions` only covers SNAPSHOT, version ranges, and LATEST/RELEASE — milestone/alpha/beta/RC versions are not "dynamic" by Maven's definition and are explicitly out of scope for this rule.
- `bannedDependencies`' wildcard support only replaces a *whole* segment (groupId, artifactId, or version) or accepts a real Maven version range. It does not support partial substring matching within the version field (e.g. `*-M*`). I verified this directly: testing both a `regex:`-prefixed pattern and a plain wildcard pattern against this version position either matched nothing, or — more concerningly — matched every dependency in the project regardless of actual version. Full test output available on request.
- I found one precedent within the OpenMRS ecosystem (openmrs-module-camel's JMS-spec ban) using `bannedDependencies` successfully, but only to ban specific named libraries outright (with a bare `*` for "any version") — not to pattern-match version content across arbitrary dependencies. This confirms the same limitation.

I'd appreciate guidance on how to handle the other pre-release qualifiers

### 4. Activating the SNAPSHOT check on the real release path (.github/workflows/release.yaml)

Per @jwnas

rows.excerpt:
owasp-java-encoder) from 1.4.1 to 1.5.0.
Release notes

Sourced from org.owasp.encoder:encoder's releases.

OWASP Java Encoder 1.5.0

Version 1.5.0 is available from Maven Central. All nine binary/source/Javadoc JARs, four POMs, and their thirteen signatures were downloaded from Central and verified against the retained signed release files. There is no encoder-esapi:1.5.0 release.

Security and correctness

  • Fixes encoded fragments completing outer HTML or XML parser delimiters across trusted-text boundaries in JavaScript HTML/block, CDATA, and XML-comment contexts. Versions through 1.4.1 are affected. See GHSA-g8p6-7r8f-qrpv.
  • Fixes EncodedWriter close/finalization behavior, exception handling, and overflow-safe array-slice validation.
  • Adds JSON encoding APIs and matching JSP/Jakarta tags and EL functions, plus XML 1.1 bindings.

Compatibility and migration

Public Java APIs remain binary and source compatible with 1.4.1 for the three supported libraries. Java 8 remains the minimum runtime; packaged consumers passed on Java 8, 11, 17, 21, and 25.

The security fixes deliberately change some encoded output:

  • JavaScript HTML/block modes emit additional hexadecimal escapes while preserving the string value. Review byte snapshots, cache keys, signatures, and output-size budgets.
  • CDATA preserves parsed text but can expand to 13 output characters per input character and can change parser event boundaries.
  • XML-comment hyphens become ~ under the documented lossy policy.

The optional ESAPI adapter is retired. Version 1.4.1 is its final published release and is unsupported; migrate to direct Java Encoder APIs. Mixing the 1.4.1 adapter with the 1.5 core is not a supported migration.

See the migration notes, ESAPI retirement guide, and
